name: Ordoliberalism
summary: Ordoliberalism holds that a competitive market is not self-sustaining but depends on a legal 'economic constitution' that the state must create and defend: it bans cartels and privileges, protects private property and contract, keeps money stable and policy rule-bound. The state shapes the rules of the game but does not steer economic processes, rejecting both laissez-faire and planning. It underlay West Germany's social market economy, with social security accepted as a complement to competition.
scope: The Freiburg School of Walter Eucken, Franz Böhm and Hans Großmann-Doerth and the postwar social market economy (Erhard), with Wilhelm Röpke's more conservative, Christian-communitarian strand. Statements on culture, religion, immigration and foreign policy are mostly outside the school and answered low-confidence; Röpke and the jurists differ on welfare and unions.

keyFigures.name: Walter Eucken
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Freiburg School and author of the principles of the competitive order

keyFigures.name: Franz Böhm
keyFigures.role: Jurist co-founder of the Freiburg School who developed the private law society and anti-privilege doctrine

keyFigures.name: Wilhelm Röpke
keyFigures.role: Economist associated with the school who called it liberal conservatism and shaped the social market economy debate

sources.title: Walter Eucken's principles of the competitive order
sources.author: Law & Liberty
sources.usedFor: Eucken constitutive and regulative principles: price system, property, free trade, stable money, liability, checks and balances, minimum wages and unions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Eucken valued social security but Röpke attacked the cradle-to-grave welfare state, so the school gives no settled view on state-provided healthcare; inferred from that split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Minimum wages are listed as acceptable in principle, but Röpke blames union and wage pressure for inflation, so a substantial rise is not an ordoliberal aim; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: A free, efficient price system is Eucken's fundamental principle and Röpke rejects planning in favour of price and competition, though both insist the market needs a legal framework.

public-ownership.rationale: Ordoliberals favoured privatising telecoms and similar firms and Röpke counts nationalization among socialism's failures, though natural monopolies may be supervised by the state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wikipedia links the school to progressive taxation, but no source gives a stance on significantly higher rates on the wealthy, and Röpke defended property; treated as split.

unions-good.rationale: Eucken accepted unions within market limits, while Röpke repeatedly attacks union monopoly power over wages; adherents are split on whether they are simply good.

property-fundamental.rationale: Protection of private property is a constitutive principle for Eucken and Röpke calls property the pillar of the free order and warns against its erosion.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Cartels and concentrations of private power must be restrained by competition law, but the aim is a rule-based framework rather than general regulation of firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Röpke argues the welfare state stifles responsibility and has outlived its need, while Eucken and the social market economy kept social security; adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Röpke wants property spread widely to individuals and independent small firms, not collective ownership of enterprises; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the school both wants a strong state and tight limits on state discretion, so the answer is inferred as split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not an ordoliberal topic; no basis in sources beyond general liberal presumptions versus Röpke's conservatism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the school; its rule-of-law stress cuts both ways, so inferred as split.

strong-leader.rationale: The 'strong state' means a state constrained by constitutional rules against interest-group capture, explicitly not an authoritarian one, and power must be checked.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is assigned the role of guardian of the competitive order and shaper of the economic constitution, so the school rejects anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the school; no basis for a firm answer.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed apart from the demand for a state able to enforce rules; inferred as neutral.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Röpke's conservatism and liberal market views point in opposite directions.

decide-locally.rationale: Röpke champions decentralization and small communities as counterweights to concentration, and ordoliberals distrust concentrated state power.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside the school's concerns; no basis for a position.

traditional-family.rationale: Röpke stresses the family and small communities as the base of a healthy society, but the Freiburg jurists said little about it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the founding generation; Röpke's conservatism and later liberal parties diverge.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Röpke's Christian outlook and liberal individualism differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Röpke deplores secularization and sees Christian tradition as the moral base of a free economy, but this is not shared across the Freiburg school.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the privilege-free, equal-legal-status ideal, which opposes group-based preferences.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Röpke values cultural inheritance and Western Christian civilization; the Freiburg jurists wrote little on national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Röpke calls himself liberal-conservative and values stability, and Eucken stresses consistent policy, but the school is about constitutional design more than pace.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The school wants an international order of rules and open trade but not obviously empowered bodies like the UN; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Open markets and free trade are a constitutive principle, and Eucken noted that many cartels would vanish if tariffs went.

nation-first.rationale: Röpke prizes international economic cooperation and convertibility, so putting national interest ahead of it is out of line; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military policy is outside the school's scope.

open-borders.rationale: Free movement of goods and money is central, but Röpke's emphasis on community makes open borders unlikely; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Growth is welcomed through competition, with environmental externalities handled by regulative principles; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Eucken's regulative principles cover external costs, which supports rule-based environmental policy, but drastic action is not addressed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Röpke is sceptical of technocratic optimism and mass civilization; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The school's emphasis on rule of law and constitutional order implies opposition, though revolution is not discussed.

experts-over-public.rationale: The school prefers rules to discretion, including independent central banks, but also ties legitimacy to citizens' consent; inferred as split.

central-planning.rationale: Eucken and the Freiburg school rejected the centrally administered economy, citing Soviet socialism and Nazism as negative examples.

socialized-markets.rationale: Röpke's property-based order is incompatible with public or worker ownership of firms; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Progressive taxation is associated with the school but heavy inheritance taxes are not documented; Röpke values family property.

basic-income.rationale: Minimum provision is accepted, but an unconditional income is not documented and sits poorly with the liability principle; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Böhm lists protective duties as privileges that violate the competitive order, and Eucken said tariffs foster cartels.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ordnungspolitik rejects discretionary industrial policy: governments cannot pick winners and invite rent-seeking.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Röpke wants a broad class of independent small and medium owners and blames concentration for destroying it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Money, prices and property are the basis of the competitive order and Röpke defends them.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: An independent central bank pursuing monetary stability is a core part of the model.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The school opposes interest-group privileges and group-made rules; wages are left to employers and unions without state-set prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ordoliberals call for a constitutionally limited state with checks against arbitrary power and condemned Nazism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Freiburg school wrote about the economic constitution and a democratic constitutional state, not about the form of head of state, so no position is documented.

democracy-best.rationale: Böhm pairs the private law society with a democratically structured constitutional state, though the school distrusts interest-group politics.

direct-votes.rationale: The school fears pressure groups swaying legislation, which suggests caution about direct votes; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power rests on a constitution with checks, not on class councils; inferred from the school's constitutional approach.

right-to-secede.rationale: None of the opened sources discuss secession; the school's concern is the economic and legal order within a state, so it is left neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; privilege-free order cuts against, Röpke's elitism for.

war-builds-character.rationale: Röpke's humane liberalism and the school's postwar orientation point strongly against; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Röpke wants Christian moral foundations while the school has no church-state doctrine.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law is a general rule order for a private law society; scripture as source is not part of it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is the guardian of the competitive order and its legal framework, so it must provide these functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Military posture is outside the economic-constitution focus of the school and no source takes a position on it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equal legal status for all persons points against ethnic definitions; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Röpke blames class hatred and social religions, and the school rejects Marxist analysis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Eucken allowed redistribution when outcomes become socially unacceptable but aims at a competitive order, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are not discussed; the school's equal-legal-status ideal and its property protection pull in different directions here.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The liability principle is about individual choices; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Röpke wrote of Western civilization but no source states a call for political union of civilizations, so neutral.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rules channel self-interest toward good ends, but Röpke insists markets need a moral base beyond supply and demand.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Röpke stresses community while the Freiburg jurists stress individual rights under law; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Eucken's external-cost principle treats nature as an economic externality, but no source takes a view on intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal and Christian leanings.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Röpke criticizes mass society and concentration but welcomes the market economy's prosperity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Röpke fears disruption of community and tradition; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics and enhancement technologies are not covered by any source on the school; left neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule-bound policy is favoured but algorithmic discretion is not discussed; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The school never addressed digital privacy or state access to communications, so no position can be documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: Röpke is culturally conservative but the school is constitution-building, not restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Vanberg stresses principles and rules over case-by-case discretion and consequences, the core of Ordnungspolitik.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional, rule-based approach.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ordoliberals focus on the legal order rather than on prefigurative methods of political change; no stance documented.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Röpke defends civilization and market economy; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Market exchange depends on specialization; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Competitive prices and performance competition, not need, distribute goods.

production-for-use.rationale: Röpke defends profit and competition as justified instruments of the market order.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Röpke calls ownership, profit and competition justified and rejects socialism's technique.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with a constitutional, privilege-free order and with Röpke's anti-collectivism.

collective-farming.rationale: Röpke favours dispersed independent owners and rejects collectivism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Röpke argues collectivism, not the market, causes disorder, and values international economic cooperation.

taxation-theft.rationale: The school gives the state a legitimate role in funding the framework and accepts progressive taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal in spirit but Röpke's conservatism complicates it; not addressed directly.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Equal rights of persons under private law are central, but group questions are not discussed.

conscription.rationale: Military service is not addressed in the sources opened, and liberal and conservative strands would differ.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Legitimacy rests on consent and constitutional order, not exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a constitutional guardian of rules, not a firm; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is framed as a competitive legal order and liability for one's choices, though minimum provision is accepted; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: The school did not make claims about universities or media holding political power, so neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Eucken grounds the order on persons as ends in themselves; no position stated, inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Böhm opposes pressure-group influence on legislation, which makes functional representation unattractive; inferred.

total-state.rationale: The school defined itself against Nazism and Soviet socialism and wants a state that shapes rules, not economic processes.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from constitutional liberalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; opposed by the school's postwar liberal orientation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The founders prized the break from feudal privilege to a private law society of equals.

bound-labor.rationale: Equal legal status and freedom of contract replace feudal bondage in their account.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Röpke trusts reason and universal civilization; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Eucken grounds the order in persons as ends in themselves and Röpke in classical and Christian tradition; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Competitive order is treated as a public good yet interest groups are expected; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The statement concerns a nationalist question the Freiburg school never addressed; no documented position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship and diaspora rights fall outside the school's economic and constitutional concerns; no position documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is not covered in any source on ordoliberalism, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Röpke prefers independent property owners; co-determination is not part of the founders' program.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Keynesian demand management is a named negative example and rules over discretion in fiscal and monetary policy is central.

economic-freedom.rationale: Ordoliberals hold that economic power turns into political power, and Röpke says the market order underpins freedom and rule of law.

rule-by-example.rationale: The school wants government bound by general rules rather than relying on rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: The school is silent on nationalism; its stress on a rule-based order is compatible with both views.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of force abroad is outside the school's scope and the sources do not address it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Röpke defends religious and cultural foundations of civilization.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility by citizenship is not discussed; Eucken accepted social security but did not specify who qualifies.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Röpke argues welfare erodes responsibility and incentives; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Röpke condemns class hatred and the school gives employers and unions joint roles in wage setting.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Röpke defends inherited cultural institutions as part of the social fabric.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from Röpke's Western, market-oriented outlook.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether labour organizes nationally or internationally is not addressed; the school is hostile to class politics generally but offers no view on this.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed by the Freiburg jurists; Röpke is conservative on family.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest and credit are part of the price system; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: A privilege-free order gives all persons the same legal status.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is meant to be guardian of the competitive order against privilege.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy supply policy is not addressed; external-cost principles would favour pricing emissions, not setting production goals.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed beyond Röpke's emphasis on community.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no place in the school; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not discussed in the sources; ordoliberal constitutional thought gives no clear preference.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional, non-expansionist outlook.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the school's individualist and conservative outlook.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The school warns politicians yield to pressure groups, but does not call elites corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Persons as ends in themselves; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The founders distanced themselves from laissez-faire and gave the state an active role in shaping the economic constitution.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal legal status and freedom of contract oppose it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal legal status for all persons and persons as ends in themselves are founding ideas.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist internal dispute; adherents reject socialism altogether.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The school did not discuss the colonial character of settler states, so no documented position.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal legal status of all under private law implies uniform civil law; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Röpke values Christian foundations but the school has no education policy on religious instruction; split and undocumented.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Vanberg says citizens' consent is the measure of legitimacy of the economic constitution.

trade-surplus.rationale: Open trade is valued for competition, not as mercantilist aim; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state must enforce rules, but private coercion such as cartels is condemned; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Performance competition is central, but struggle between peoples is not part of it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from postwar German constitutional order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The school's worry about private economic power limiting others' liberty fits this idea.

separated-powers.rationale: Eucken's political order includes checks and balances against arbitrary power.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Eucken accepts social security and justice but not a priority claim.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Fits Röpke's wide-spread property ideal; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Röpke attacks union monopoly power; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Neither the Freiburg jurists nor Röpke in the opened text address ethnic diversity and cohesion directly.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rule-of-law emphasis opposes discretionary suspension; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A free price system is fundamental and Erhard lifted price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from liberal opposition to totalitarian control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from constitutional limits on power.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed by the school; no basis for a position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not addressed; the school's concern is rules against privilege, which is compatible with either answer.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party organization is outside the school's concerns; no source states a view.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The school wants rule-based European order but ordoliberals split on supranational union.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not an ordoliberal topic, and no position is documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Checks on power imply term limits; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not discussed; Böhm's worry about pressure groups cuts both ways on this tool.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not addressed by the school; postwar West German practice favoured alliances but no source states it as doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Röpke praises village and small-town life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National division and reunification are not addressed in the opened sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The school made no claims about the outlook of educated people; Röpke's criticism of intellectualization is too general to infer a view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Röpke defends Western Christian civilization; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Liability for one's own choices is a constitutive principle, and the school favours no-bailout rules.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Procedure for writing a constitution is not discussed, though Vanberg notes consent as the test of legitimacy of the economic constitution.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economic transformation is not addressed; the school would back market and legal reform but not a property overhaul, leaving it neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The school sees economic and political order as interdependent.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: International aid duties are not addressed; Röpke discusses underdeveloped countries but the opened passages do not state a duty of aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is outside the school's concerns and no source states a position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The institutional design of the presidency is not discussed; the school has no stated view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Politically independent central banks focused on price stability are a defining ordoliberal principle, reflected in Maastricht.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes are not covered by the school, so no documented position.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is defended as a pillar of the order, not conditionally; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents call it collectivist; the specific debate is not addressed.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Externality regulation is accepted but a precaution rule is not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The school gave no doctrine on annexation; its rule-of-law outlook suggests sympathy but nothing is stated.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A ceremonial head of state is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession and military force are not addressed by the school, so neutral.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy inside a larger state is not discussed; Röpke's decentralization supports autonomy but nothing is stated on this case.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wikipedia associates the school with progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: The school offers no theory of human nature beyond treating persons as ends in themselves, so no position documented.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Government by general rules and constitutional limits is the core of Ordnungspolitik.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not addressed by any ordoliberal source and is wholly anachronistic.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Checks and balances are endorsed, but the ancient doctrine of mixing few and many is not discussed; left neutral.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law on custody is not addressed by the school, so no documented position.

land-redistribution.rationale: Röpke wants widespread property but not expropriation; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are outside the school's concerns; no source states a view.

common-currency.rationale: Ordoliberals favour rule-based monetary union but are split on the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national union by kinship is not discussed; the school's rule-based internationalism points elsewhere but nothing is stated.

death-penalty.rationale: The school has no penal doctrine; the emphasis on equal legal status, limited state discretion and a constrained strong state suggests wariness of the death penalty, but this is an inference.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: No source addresses school curricula; Röpke's conservatism and liberal individualism pull in different directions.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Röpke's Christian outlook is balanced by his trust in reason and the market-economy scholarship, so a mild inference against.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Röpke's cultural conservatism would favour limits while liberal ordoliberals would not.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed in any source on the school; neutral.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is outside the school's concerns and not addressed in the sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Equal legal status under general rules is a founding principle, so exemptions from general laws look like privileges; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Röpke values tradition and community while liberal strands welcome nonconformity; no source takes a stand.

ban-cartels.rationale: Banning cartels and curbing private economic power is the defining task of the state as guardian of the competitive order.

no-bailouts.rationale: Liability for each actor's own choices is a constitutive principle and Vanberg cites bailouts as discretionary interventions to be denied.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Outside the school; no position on minority cultural institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Outside the school; no position on minority emigration versus rights struggles.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Eucken rejected historicist and economic-determinist accounts, holding that the legal and political order shapes the economy and not the reverse.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Ordoliberalism rests on a constitutional framework binding even democratic majorities, with law and an independent judiciary protecting the competitive order.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; the emphasis on equal legal status and privilege-free order argues against group quotas, inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Eucken's principles require open markets and free trade, and autarky and protectionism are rejected as privileges and distortions.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed directly; the school favours free trade governed by general rules and distrusts discretionary political conditions, inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: The competitive price system, with private property and liability, is the coordinating mechanism; replacing material incentives is the opposite of the programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The school builds a lawful order through constitutional means and Roepke warns against collectivist upheaval, so revolution by arms is rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A privilege-free order with equal legal status is a core aim; Boehm opposed granting privileges, so hereditary privileges fall under that, though titles themselves are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Outside the school; ordoliberals wrote on economic order, and Röpke's conservative strand differs from the jurists.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to a privilege-free order and equal legal status, and Röpke's wariness of centralized power; not addressed directly.

patriotic-education.rationale: Outside the school; Röpke valued community and tradition while the Freiburg jurists focused on economic constitution, so views split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the privilege-free order and equal legal status for all, which tells against group preferences; not addressed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Ordoliberals want an independent central bank bound by rules for stable money, not discretionary state creation of money; commercial banking itself is accepted within that frame.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: the school holds a competitive order can endure if the legal framework is kept, while warning that cartels and Keynesian discretion cause crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on rule-bound, open trade over political spheres of influence; not addressed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Eucken's principles favor free trade and open markets as part of the competitive order.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the school sees competitive markets with equal legal status as serving all workers and has no exploitation theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The school stresses freedom of contract but also equal legal status and bans on privilege; it did not address anti-discrimination law, so inferred as split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Ordoliberals want an economic constitution that binds the state and is protected from political discretion, supporting entrenched guarantees such as property and contract.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; the legal order and contract stability the school stresses are inferred to weigh against voiding treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: A rule-bound constitutional state is inferred to be chosen by election, not heredity.

minority-veto.rationale: Rules agreed constitutionally bind everyone; a general dissenter veto is inferred as unworkable for the school.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Eucken and Böhm place the state under law; resistance to lawbreaking rulers is inferred from the checks and balances principle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The school wants rules binding discretionary lawmaking, with independent central banks and fixed constitutional principles.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; Röpke stresses humane values, so recognition of animal suffering is inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; humane use is the inferred mainstream view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Röpke grounds the market in Christian and communal obligation; duty of the better-off is inferred from that.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Röpke stresses citizenship and community, so withdrawal from public life is inferred as contrary.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Röpke criticizes mass society and massification but not in terms of pacification to reproduce the social order; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The school sees power as concentrated by cartels and privilege, not mainly by cultural consent; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Open markets and free trade are core principles of the competitive order, so extraction theories are rejected.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal legal status without privilege is inferred to oppose birth-based reservation of offices.

party-own-road.rationale: Indifferent to how socialist parties organize; the school opposes planning.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Open trade and investment are inferred as the school's preferred route to development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; the postwar social market order was built on renouncing revanchism, inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal legal status is inferred to oppose ancestry-based leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Freiburg School thinkers opposed the Nazi state, and anti-fascism is inferred as consistent with the postwar order.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Eucken rejected centrally administered economies of every kind, covering both Nazi and Soviet types.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; accepting the historical consensus is inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are inferred to be split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equality before the law is inferred to favor equal protection.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The school treats its rule-of-law order as generally valid; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A rule-bound constitutional state with civilian authority is inferred to exclude a political guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Röpke's family-centered communitarianism favors family provision over wage-based care work; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Röpke's humane economy depends on strong families as a moral base for the market; inferred from his communitarian strand.

office-by-exam.rationale: The school addresses the economic order, not how public posts are filled; adherents are split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The competitive order rests on open markets and equal rules for all firms, so blocking foreign buyers is inferred to be disfavoured, though the state may defend competition.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Röpke's conservative strand favours stable marriage while the jurists were liberal; the school did not address it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The school favours a rule-bound state and constitutional limits, so delegates bound to constituents' will are inferred to be disfavoured.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Ordoliberals accept social security as a complement to competition and differ on how to organise it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property is one of Eucken's constituting principles of the competitive order, so communal land with use-based tenure is rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The economic constitution is a rule-bound public framework, so parliamentary authorisation of spending is inferred to be accepted.

single-official-language.rationale: The school did not address language policy; adherents are split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The competitive order assumes open markets and secure property for all participants, so a blanket ban on foreign land ownership is inferred to be disfavoured.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The school emphasises equal rules for all and non-discrimination in the competitive order, not outcome-based tests; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Röpke's A Humane Economy criticises mass society and materialism as eroding the moral base of the free market.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The school stresses rule-bound policy and law; covert arming of insurgents is inferred to be disfavoured.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The school's rule-bound order and Röpke's liberal internationalism imply that forcible intervention against an ally is disfavoured; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ordoliberals saw interest-group and corporate capture of the state as a core threat to the competitive order, which is why they want an economic constitution that keeps privileges and cartels out of policy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal, open-economy outlook; it did not address foreign funding of NGOs or media.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Röpke valued the family, but the school's rule-bound, non-steering state makes targeted fertility incentives a point on which adherents are split; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to free movement of capital and secure private property under general rules, which sit badly with local purchase limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Ordoliberals put monetary stability ahead of employment targets and reject state steering of the economy, so an employer-of-last-resort scheme runs against the framework.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from Röpke's liberal internationalism; the school did not address the democratic-peace thesis directly.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the central place of the rule of law and legal order in the school's thinking, which leaves little room for a right to disregard law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by the school; inferred from its rule-based, liberal-internationalist outlook.

industrial-unions.rationale: Ordoliberals worried about union monopoly power distorting the competitive order, so they would not favour industry-wide union structures; jurists and Röpke differ.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The liberal, rule-of-law outlook rejects collective suspicion of minorities; the school never addressed it, so this is inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Röpke's Christian-communitarian strand defends the family and the legal order around it; inferred, as the school's economists did not address marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on transparent, rule-bound and predictable policy; not a stated doctrine.

local-production.rationale: The school defends competitive markets and the division of labour, though Röpke favoured decentralisation and small-scale units; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The school stresses formal legal frameworks and institutions; inferred from its constitutional orientation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Ordoliberalism strongly shaped the supranational European economic and competition constitution, so adherents tend not to put national law above it; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Röpke was Christian but the school's liberal framework does not define the nation by religion; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Eucken favored free trade and a privilege-free order with equal legal status; inferred that ritual submission has no place in it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The liability principle ties decisions to their costs, which favors regions keeping their own revenue; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Ordoliberals defend private property and contract and Röpke opposed nationalization, so common ownership of productive property is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Röpke was a forceful critic of collectivism and communism, and the school was formed against totalitarian planning.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Ordoliberals accept social provision within a competitive framework, which allows private providers; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Röpke grounded the free economy in Christian and communitarian values, so a materialist account of religion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Competitive market economy is endorsed, though Röpke criticized mass society and concentration; the answer is inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The school gives no program on gender; its focus on legal order and family and community suggests reform within it; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Röpke criticized the cradle-to-grave welfare state and prized the family and small communities; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is outside the school and conflicts with its liberal open order; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Rule-bound policy and the Rechtsstaat favor stable, binding commitments; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Röpke valued small communities but kept private property and markets, so common ownership is not endorsed; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-steered settlement is intervention in processes the school wants left to rules and competition; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ordoliberalism calls itself a third way between laissez-faire and planning, but it takes the market economy as the sound basis, so it does not accept the statement as framed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ordoliberalism's rule-of-law, equal-status order favors present holders' rights over historical claims; inferred, the school never addressed it.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Freiburg School grew out of resistance to Nazi rule and the school rejects totalitarian falsehood; denial is incompatible with its liberal humanism, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; Eucken's liberal order disfavors state coercion in private life, while conservative Röpke tempers this, so mild disagreement is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The economic constitution is a privilege-free, rule-bound order with equal legal status, which is incompatible with suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Röpke was Christian-communitarian but the school builds a constrained, rule-bound state; inferred disagreement.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The school stresses free trade and equal competition without privilege, which contradicts running colonies for the metropole; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Outside the school entirely; inferred disagreement from its secular, state-centered rule-based order.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The school wants a legal order bound by rules, not by religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ordoliberals favor a strong, rule-bound state and expert-framed economic constitution over direct workplace and community decision-making; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not part of the school; inferred from its individualist, class-neutral competitive order.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative, communitarian side of the school (Röpke).

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal and Christian-conservative strands of the school would split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The school defines itself as a third way between laissez-faire and planning, which suggests combining ideas from both sides; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Röpke criticized proletarianization and mass society, but the school does not blame capitalism as such; adherents are mixed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Röpke's emphasis on a Christian-Western cultural basis for a free economy.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Röpke was religious, but the school grounds the state in an economic constitution and rule of law, not divine authority; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's preference for limiting state coercion.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The school favors rules that protect competition and equal legal status but also contractual freedom; no stated view.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ordoliberalism underlay West Germany's social market economy, combining competition rules with social security.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The school assumes a state that defends the legal order; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: The privilege-free order demands equal conditions of competition, which sits uneasily with letting some get ahead first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Postwar ordoliberals around Erhard supported integration with the West; inferred, the sources do not address blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ordoliberalism opposes privileges and concentrated power under a legal economic constitution; hereditary rule is inferred to be excluded.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The school wants competition under rules and stable money; it does not endorse user-owned cost-price credit, though cooperative banks fit its decentralism. Inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Ordoliberals insist on rule-bound, stable fiscal and monetary policy, so conditions that enforce discipline are broadly accepted.

property-franchise.rationale: Eucken's principles stress equal rules for all; no wealth test is advocated. Inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Outside the school's concerns; Röpke's communitarian humanism is critical of mass society but does not frame it as domination. Inferred.

reification.rationale: Ordoliberals treat markets as a framework the state must design, not as a mystifying force; the idea is a Marxist one. Inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Ordoliberals worry about private concentrations of power, but regard press and assembly rights as real; inferred from their anti-cartel stance.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Eucken's constituting principles call for constancy and predictability of rule-bound policy, and the school stresses rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The school's equal-rules liberal order excludes ethnic privileges; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed by the school; adherents could go either way. Inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: A rule-bound state under public scrutiny fits ordoliberal order; inferred, not stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage law is outside the school, and its liberal legal order points against religious restrictions; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Röpke's conservative strand is culturally traditional, yet the school's liberal order disfavours targeting by religion. Inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The school wanted a rule-bound economic constitution kept above shifting popular majorities, so it leans toward law and expertise over lay deliberation; inferred, as the question was never addressed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Roepke wrote from a conservative Christian standpoint while the Freiburg jurists were largely silent on doctrine, so no school view exists; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Freiburg School held that concentrated private economic power undermines the competitive order and freedom, and wanted the state to break it up.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the school; inferred from its liberal, rule-of-law legal order that treats citizens equally.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not addressed directly; the state is to shape the rules of the economy, not belief, and Röpke's Christian humanism opposes official atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ordoliberalism makes the strong state the guardian of law and order and the competitive framework.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the school favors a strong, rule-bound state and federal order but said little about communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Röpke stressed community and subsidiarity, but social security is accepted as a complement to competition, so adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; a rule-bound constitutional order is valued but term limits are not part of the school.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the school wants a strong, expert-guided constitutional state, and Röpke distrusted mass democratic politics.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Outside the school; no stated position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Outside the school; Röpke's Christian strand is conservative, the jurists silent, so split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Outside the school; Röpke valued the traditional family but the Freiburg jurists did not address it, so split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ordoliberalism did not address local voting rights; Röpke's communitarian strand leans against while the liberal strand is indifferent, so it is split.

rent-control.rationale: Ordoliberals hold that prices must form freely in competition and reject price controls; Eucken's principles of the competitive order favor the price system, and rent caps distort it.

abolish-ip.rationale: Eucken's school opposes privileges and monopolies, which could cast patents as suspect, but it also protects private property under the economic constitution; abolition is inferred as rejected by most.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ordoliberalism, formed against totalitarianism, sets limits on the state; Röpke's conservative strand values youth education but not drilled state movements; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing was outside the school's concerns; no stated position exists.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign policy was outside the school; the postwar German social market economy accepted allied basing, but ordoliberals took no stated position.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Ordoliberalism emerged from rejecting Nazi totalitarianism and Röpke wrote on moral order; support for formal recognition of mass crimes is inferred rather than stated.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Eucken accepted social security and competition rewards performance, but the school defends property income as part of the competitive order; the sources show it split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ordoliberals hold that the state must protect persons and order and Röpke's Christian humanism accepts self-defence; inferred as disfavoring an absolute ban.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ordoliberalism is a theory of economic order and does not rest on national origin myths; Röpke was cosmopolitan and anti-collectivist, so this claim is inferred as disfavored.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gender theory is outside the Freiburg School; no position exists.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Ordoliberalism does not address feminist politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Röpke's anti-collectivism and focus on a humane economy make state-sponsored martyr cults unlikely; inferred as disfavored.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Ordoliberalism concerns the legal order of the economy; Röpke held a spiritual view of civilization, but the school did not frame politics as a struggle of good against evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora and homeland roles are not addressed by the school.

culture-before-state.rationale: Röpke argued that moral and cultural foundations underpin the market, but the Freiburg jurists put the economic constitution first, so the school is split.

god-not-male.rationale: Ordoliberalism has no stated view on how God is described; adherents are split by personal belief.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Ordoliberalism does not address how religious texts should be judged.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ordoliberalism requires a privilege-free competitive order open to all, so reserving economic life for a national majority contradicts equal competition and the ban on privileges.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The school did not address ethnic territorial units; its general-rules, individual-rights approach makes group territories disfavored by inference.

independent-unions.rationale: The sources note the school split on unions, with concern about union market power balanced by freedom of association.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ordoliberals reject planning and state steering, but did not discuss what makes a society socialist.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Eucken allowed state regulation of natural monopolies, but the school mainly favours competition elsewhere; adherents split.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the school's constitutional emphasis on rule-bound policy is compatible with either arrangement.

municipal-property.rationale: Private property and contract are protected pillars of the competitive order, and the school rejects collective ownership as well as planning.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The school wants a strong state that enforces the rules of the economic constitution rather than weak coordinating bodies. Inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Wages are set within competitive markets with social security as a complement, not by household need, though Röpke's strand is more sympathetic to families. Inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; stable money is a principle, but nothing on payment privacy.

person-over-state.rationale: Röpke's A Humane Economy and the school's concern for the dignity and freedom of the person treat the economy as serving people.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Röpke's Christian humanism holds that the market economy must be embedded in moral and spiritual foundations.

dense-cities.rationale: Röpke favoured decentralised, smaller-scale settlement and criticised mass concentration, but this is inferred and not central.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The school defends equal legal order and individual freedom, which tells against organising by racial group. Inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed by the school; postwar German ordoliberals worked in a defensive-only setting but gave no principle.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The school is about economic order and has no theory of nationhood; I inferred mild disagreement from its liberal, rule-of-law outlook.

communal-electorates.rationale: Ordoliberals want a privilege-free order with equal rules for all, which suggests common electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nothing in the school supports claims of foreign plots, and it favored postwar Western integration under Erhard; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Röpke was skeptical of mass higher education and the school stresses individual responsibility, though postwar Germany funded universities; the sources do not address tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Eucken's liability principle holds that actors should bear the costs of their actions, and ordoliberals prefer market-conforming instruments to discretionary intervention.

future-generations.rationale: Röpke's humane economy emphasizes continuity and responsibility to coming generations; this is inferred from his communitarian strand.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The school has no position on gender and favors equal general rules; Röpke's conservatism makes agreement unlikely; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The school did not address armaments and adherents would likely accept defense as a core state task without a view on cuts.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Ordnungspolitik stresses transparent rules for the economy but the school never discussed treaty secrecy.

capital-controls.rationale: Eucken wanted a stable, convertible currency within an open competitive order, which implies free capital movement; the sources do not discuss controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The ordoliberal state is strong and enforces the legal order; inferred, with no explicit statement on private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on state authority and the legal order; the school did not address conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Eucken accepted unions but warned against labour monopolies as cartels, and Röpke was harsher; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Eucken accepted redistribution within the competitive order, while Röpke opposed expansive welfare; the school is split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Rule-bound policy and stable money are core principles of the competitive order, and the German debt brake draws on them.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the school's focus on competition and rules rather than preferential interventions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The ordoliberal state is meant to be strong and to guard the order, not to be destroyed; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Eucken's principles define one competitive order and reject mixing economic systems, so there is no open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Röpke valued nature and tradition but proposed no pricing scheme.

sacred-nation.rationale: Röpke defended national and local community but not as sacred; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the stress on liability for one's own choices.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the view that regional gaps are met by competition and rules rather than exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Röpke's Christian humanism treats the person as a moral being; inferred from A Humane Economy.

public-service-media.rationale: The school did not address public broadcasting; Röpke criticised mass culture while the German system emerged under the social market.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ordoliberalism is an economic school with no view on religious truth, although Röpke was Christian.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Freiburg School opposed privileges, subsidies and tariffs for particular groups, which counts against price guarantees; Röpke accepted some farm protection, so low confidence.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The school did not address it and is silent on nuclear policy.

workers-own-party.rationale: Ordoliberals oppose group power over markets, including union power, and want a state above group interests; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The state as guardian of an order of equal legal status implies protecting persons from harm; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Eucken's order rests on equal legal status and private property for all; inferred support for equal rights.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Eucken's liability principle makes polluters answer for harm, but ordoliberals favour state rules that set the framework, not only lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Ordoliberals want a strong state under constitutional rule and elected lawmaking; a formal role for chiefs is inferred as outside it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ordoliberals favour state rules that internalise external costs, but Röpke also defended freedom and community; split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The school favours rules over discretion in the economic sphere, but did not address sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Röpke's communitarian strand values a shared culture, so a language requirement is inferred as acceptable.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Eucken opposed concentrations of private power including union monopolies, though the school did not settle this; inferred from that.

voter-id.rationale: Outside the school; no settled view on ballot identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; liberal neutrality pulls one way and Röpke's Christian communitarian strand the other.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The school wants a strong rule-bound state constraining even majorities, so it treats elections as necessary but not sufficient; adherents split, inferred from that.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; Röpke's conservative strand and the liberal jurists differ.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on rule-bound state action and limits on discretionary power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The school accepts social security as a complement to competition but never endorsed replacing welfare programs with one payment; inferred from that.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the commitment to equal legal rules for all participants in the order.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; Röpke in particular valued religion as a moral basis of the free market.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the commitment to equal general rules rather than group privileges.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the preference for general rules over targeted state intervention.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its focus on the legal framework of competition, not on the origin of property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on international criminal justice.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the school's focus on economic order; Röpke's Christianity does not imply literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on group self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Eucken and Röpke reject central planning as incompatible with a competitive order and with freedom, so a planned state is not worth defending for its system.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its focus on the economic constitution rather than electoral design.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from Röpke's Christian outlook against the jurists' silence; strands differ.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on ethnic autonomy; Röpke's decentralism points one way, the school's silence the other.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on post-colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Röpke's A Humane Economy criticises mass consumption and materialism and favours small-scale, self-reliant life; inferred from that, and not shared by the jurists.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on settlement policy.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from its silence on conscription.

missingStatements.text: The state should prohibit cartels and break up concentrations of economic power in order to protect competition.
missingStatements.rationale: Banning cartels and curbing private economic power is the defining task of the state as guardian of the competitive order.

missingStatements.text: Governments should not grant special privileges, such as subsidies, tariffs or tax breaks, to particular firms or groups.
missingStatements.rationale: Böhm held that the state should on no account confer privileges, since this invites rent-seeking and undermines the privilege-free order.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by existing statements on tariffs-protect-industry and state-directs-investment, which ordoliberalism answers against.

missingStatements.text: Economic policy should follow fixed general rules rather than case-by-case discretion by officials.
missingStatements.rationale: Government by general rules instead of discretion is the core of Ordnungspolitik.
missingStatements.declined: Abstract rules-versus-discretion principle that nearly all ideologies would endorse in the abstract; too vague to separate ideologies.

missingStatements.text: Governments should not bail out failing banks or firms with public money.
missingStatements.rationale: Liability for each actor's own choices is a constitutive principle and Vanberg cites bailouts as discretionary interventions to be denied.

notes: Röpke and the Freiburg jurists diverge: Röpke is harsher on welfare and unions and culturally conservative, whereas Eucken accepted unions, minimum wages and redistribution within the competitive order. Source s1 is Wikipedia only for overview; the euro-crisis stance is not scored.
